parts.text: Paul blesses God for every spiritual blessing in Christ. Before the world’s foundation, God chose his people in him for holiness and appointed their adoption through Jesus. Through Christ’s blood they have redemption and forgiveness, and God has revealed his purpose to gather all things in heaven and earth in Christ. Believers receive an inheritance according to that purpose. After hearing the gospel and believing, they are sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, the pledge of their inheritance until final redemption.

Thankful for their faith and love, Paul prays that they may know God more fully and understand the hope of his calling, the riches of his inheritance, and his power toward believers. That power raised Christ and seated him above every authority, now and in the world to come. God has placed all things under him and given him as head to the church, his body.

chapters.title: Saved by grace and brought together

parts.text: Paul reminds his readers that they were dead in sins, following the world’s course and fleshly desires. Yet God’s rich mercy and love made them alive with Christ, raised them, and seated them in heavenly places in him. Salvation is God’s gift by grace through faith, not a reward for works, so no one can boast. They are nevertheless God’s workmanship, created in Christ for the good works he prepared for them to do.

Gentiles once lacked Israel’s covenant privileges, hope, and God, but Christ’s blood has brought them near. He is their peace, removing the barrier and reconciling Jew and Gentile to God in one body through the cross. Both now approach the Father by one Spirit. They are fellow citizens and members of God’s household, built on the apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone, growing into God’s dwelling through the Spirit.

chapters.title: The revealed mystery and a prayer for fullness

parts.text: Paul explains the grace entrusted to him for Gentiles: the mystery now revealed by the Spirit is that they share the inheritance, body, and promise in Christ through the gospel. Though considering himself least among the saints, he was appointed to proclaim Christ’s unsearchable riches and make known what was hidden in God. Through the church, God’s varied wisdom is displayed to heavenly powers according to his eternal purpose. Believers have confident access in Christ, and Paul asks them not to lose heart over his sufferings.

Paul prays that the Father strengthen them inwardly by the Spirit, that Christ dwell in their hearts by faith, and that they become rooted in love. He asks that they grasp Christ’s love, which surpasses knowledge, and be filled with God’s fullness. He closes by glorifying God, who can do far beyond all they ask or imagine through his power at work within them.

Paul urges a life worthy of their calling, marked by humility, patience, and loving efforts to preserve the Spirit’s unity. There is one body, Spirit, hope, Lord, faith, baptism, and Father. The ascended Christ gives different ministries to equip the saints, build his body, and bring maturity in faith and knowledge. This guards against deceptive teaching. Speaking truth in love, each member contributes to the whole body’s growth under Christ its head.

Believers must leave the darkened, callous way of life they formerly knew, putting off the corrupt old self and putting on the renewed self created in righteousness and holiness. Paul calls for truthfulness, restraint in anger, honest work that enables giving, and speech that builds others up. They must not grieve the Holy Spirit who seals them for redemption. Bitterness and malice should give way to kindness and forgiveness patterned on God’s forgiveness in Christ.

Paul urges believers to imitate God and walk in Christ’s self-giving love. Sexual immorality, greed, and degrading speech contradict their calling and incur judgment. Once darkness, they are now light in the Lord and must expose rather than join unfruitful works. They should use time wisely, understand the Lord’s will, and be filled with the Spirit instead of drunkenness, expressing worship, gratitude, and mutual submission.

Wives are instructed to submit to their husbands as the church submits to Christ. Husbands must love their wives as Christ loved and gave himself for the church, seeking its cleansing and holiness. They should nourish and cherish their wives as their own bodies. Paul relates the marriage union of one flesh to the great mystery concerning Christ and his church, concluding with the husband’s duty to love and the wife’s to reverence.

Children should obey and honor their parents, while fathers should nurture them in the Lord without provoking resentment. Servants must obey earthly masters sincerely, serving Christ rather than merely performing when watched. The Lord rewards good without regard to whether someone is bond or free. Masters likewise must act responsibly and stop threatening, remembering that both they and their servants answer to an impartial Master in heaven.

Paul calls believers to strength in the Lord and the whole armor of God against spiritual enemies. Truth, righteousness, readiness with the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and God’s word equip them to stand. They must pray continually for all saints and for Paul’s bold witness as an imprisoned ambassador of the gospel. Tychicus will bring news and encouragement. Paul closes with peace, love, faith, and grace for those sincerely loving Christ.
